source_text: Cito orationes ad Deum ascendunt quas ad Deum menta nostri operis inponunt. sic et Raphael angelus Tobiae oranti semper et semper operanti adstitit dicens: opera Dei reuelare et confiteri honorificum est. nam quando orabas tu et Sarra, ego optuli memoriam orationis uestrae in conspectu claritatis Dei: et cum sepelires tu mortuos simpliciter, et quia non es cunctatus exurgere et derelinquere prandium tuum, sed abisti et condidisti mortuum, et missus sum temptare te: et iterum me misit Deus curare te et Sarram nurum tuam. ego enim sum Raphael, unus ex septem angelis iustis qui adsistimus et conuersamur ante claritatem Dei. per Esaiam quoque Dominus admonet et docet similia contestans, solue, inquit, omnem nodum iniustitiae, resolue suffocationes inpotentium commerciorum: dimitte quassatos in requiem et omnem consignationem iniustam dissipa: frange esurienti panem tuum et egenos sine tecto induc in domum tuam: si uideris nudum, uesti et domesticos seminis tui non despicies. tunc erumpet temporaneum lumen tuum et uestimenta tua cito orientur et praeibit ante te iustitia et claritas Dei circumdabit te. tunc exclamabis, et Deus exaudiet te: dum adhuc loqueris, dicit: ecce adsum. adesse se repromittit et audire ac protegere se eos dicit qui iniustitiae nodos de corde soluentes et eleemosynas circa domesticos Dei secundum eius praecepta facientes, dum audiunt quod Deus praecipit fieri, ipsi quoque a Deo merentur audiri. beatus apostolus Paulus in necessitate pressurae adiutus a fratribus opera quae fiunt sacrificia Deo dixit esse. saturatus sum, inquit, recipiens ab Epaphrodito ea quae a uobis missa sunt, odores suauitatis, sacrificium acceptum et placitum Deo. nam quando qui miseretur pauperi, Deo faenerat et qui dat minimis Deo donat, spiritaliter Deo suauitatis odores sacrificat.
orientation: Cyprian is continuing his argument that prayer must be joined with good works, now giving examples from Raphael, Isaiah, and Paul.

choices.why: Literal rendering of menta as 'minds' (plural of mens), preserving the oddity of the source phrase rather than smoothing it into 'the mind of our work' or 'our working minds'

choices.english: dwell before the glory of God
choices.why: Conversari means to dwell, live, or keep company with, not to walk; 'dwell before' preserves the spatial sense of standing in the divine presence
rejected: walk before the glory of God
converse before the glory of God

choices.english: the chokings of the powerless in business dealings
choices.why: Inpotentium is genitive plural of inpotens, 'the powerless,' not 'oppressive'; suffocationes are stranglings or chokings, and commerciorum are business dealings, so the phrase means the choking exploitation of the weak in commerce
Orientur is from orior, to rise or dawn (like the sun), not to shine; the metaphor is of garments rising like the dawn, so 'rise' preserves the verb's force
Literal rendering of the sacrificial metaphor; 'odors' keeps the physical sense of the offering's fragrance, and 'sweetness' renders suauitas directly
Faenero means to lend at interest, but in this biblical context the sense is simply lending to God; 'lends' is the plain literal rendering without importing the financial connotation

pass_b_english: Prayers ascend quickly to God when the merits of our work place them before God. So also the angel Raphael stood by Tobit, who was always praying and always working, and said: “It is honorable to reveal and confess the works of God. For when you and Sarah were praying, I offered the remembrance of your prayer in the sight of the glory of God. And when you buried the dead simply, and because you did not hesitate to rise and leave your dinner, but went and buried the dead man, and I was sent to test you. And again God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law. For I am Raphael, one of the seven righteous angels who stand and dwell before the glory of God” (Tobit 12:12-15). Through Isaiah also the Lord admonishes and teaches, bearing witness to similar things: “Loose,” he says, “every knot of injustice, loose the bonds of contracts that strangle the powerless. Let the broken go free into rest, and scatter every unjust contract. Break your bread to the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house. If you see the naked, clothe them, and do not despise your own kin. Then your early light will break forth, and your garments will quickly shine forth, and righteousness will go before you, and the glory of God will surround you. Then you will cry out, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking, he says: Here I am” (Isaiah 58:6-9). He promises that he is present, and says that he hears and protects those who loosen the knots of injustice from their hearts and do almsgiving among God's household according to his commands. While they hear what God commands to be done, they themselves also deserve to be heard by God. The blessed apostle Paul, helped by the brothers in a time of pressing need, said that the works that are done are sacrifices to God. “I am filled,” he says, “receiving from Epaphroditus the things sent by you, odors of sweetness, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God” (Philippians 4:18). For when someone has mercy on the poor, he lends to God, and when he gives to the least, he gives to God, spiritually sacrificing to God odors of sweetness.

last_rejected.source_quote: opera Dei reuelare et confiteri honorificum est. nam quando orabas tu et Sarra
last_rejected.why: The opening sentence is Tobit 12:11; 12:12 begins only at the prayer of Tobit and Sarah.
last_rejected.ruling: The quoted passage spans Tobit 12:11–15 ("opera Dei reuelare…" through "unus ex septem angelis"). The cited range 12:12-15 is slightly short but is a minor citation imprecision, not misleading.

last_rejected.source_quote: quas ad Deum menta nostri operis inponunt
last_rejected.why: Source likely 'merita' (merits); English fine. But 'sepelires' clause: English leaves 'when you buried... and I was sent' without main verb, sense of 'et quia non es cunctatus' garbled.
last_rejected.fix: And when you buried the dead simply, and did not hesitate to rise and leave your dinner, but went and buried the dead man, I was sent to test you.
last_rejected.ruling: English follows the Latin anacoluthon: quia non es cunctatus…sed abisti et condidisti keeps its sense, and missus sum remains the finite verb.
